Heat Advisory meets coastal fog and flooding concerns
Inland heat will continue through Sunday as coastal areas face elevated evening tides and minor flooding concerns through the weekend.
Inland heat will continue through Sunday as coastal areas face elevated evening tides and minor flooding concerns through the weekend.
A heat advisory remains in effect through Sunday evening for much of the inland Central Coast, including the Santa Cruz Mountains and areas around King City, as temperatures climb above average.
The hottest locations could reach the mid-90s to around 105 degrees Sunday afternoon, with the greatest heat impacts expected farther inland and in higher elevations. Overnight temperatures will also remain unusually warm in some of the hills, while coastal communities stay considerably cooler.
Closer to Monterey and Salinas, the marine layer is quickly pushing inland this evening. That cooler, moist air will bring clouds and lower temperatures to the coast, with coastal highs generally staying in the 60s and 70s. Low clouds and fog are expected to return overnight.
There are also coastal flooding concerns through Thursday morning, particularly around the highest evening tides. Minor flooding is possible in low-lying bayshore areas around Monterey Bay, so beachgoers and anyone visiting waterfront areas should be aware of changing water levels and avoid flooded or vulnerable spots.
The combination of hot inland temperatures and dry conditions is also creating near-critical fire weather concerns in higher terrain through Sunday. Residents in the hottest areas should limit prolonged outdoor activity, stay hydrated and never leave children or pets unattended in vehicles.
Relief is expected early next week, with temperatures trending closer to seasonal averages by Monday and continuing through the middle of the week.

articles.full_text:
SATURDAY NIGHT: As a line of showers moves southeast out of our region, skies will stay partly-mostly cloudy and hazy. Temperatures will cool to lows in the 60s tonight.
SUNDAY: Hot again with highs in the 90s and 100s. Another Heat Advisory will be in place from noon to 8 PM. Skies will be mostly sunny in the morning, with more clouds in the afternoon. Chance for isolated afternoon storms, but rainfall is tracking to be minimal to due to dry surface humidity.
MONDAY: Temperatures remain in the 90s and 100s, albeit a few degrees cooler. Scattered thunderstorms likely in the afternoon.
REST OF WEEK: Temperatures will continue to cool throughout the week moving from the 90s to the 70s by the end of the week. However storm chances will inversely increase as the week progresses.
